description: We are a team of five developers and designers who enjoy building things. We started in high school, where we created SafeStep AI on our own to help people identify phishing scams. While working on this project, we were also teaching ourselves machine learning, which meant spending a lot of time going through datasets, training neural networks, and fixing mistakes until we got everything working.
summary: EVAde is a crew health monitor for astronauts on long-duration missions. It helps a crew member answer one question each day: is this reading a real change for me, or normal adaptation to spaceflight? EVAde collects vitals, sleep, mood and radiation dose, compares each with the astronaut's own baseline and with reference ranges, and rates it green, yellow or red with the reason and the next step. Expected in-flight trends and radiation limits come from NASA Human Research Program evidence reports, the NASA Twins Study, Artemis I and Curiosity RAD dosimetry, and NASA's 600 mSv career limit. Live NOAA space weather becomes a spacewalk go/no-go. A voice agent built on Twilio and xAI Grok runs the daily check-in by phone or browser and queues concerns for the flight surgeon over an ISS, Mars-delay or blackout link. EVAde gives astronauts who are not doctors a clear, explainable view of their own health far from Earth.
details:
What it does

On long missions, radiation, isolation, altered gravity and a closed environment can cause bone loss, immune changes, cardiovascular events and behavioral-health problems. Astronauts carry much of the job of noticing these changes in themselves, and most are not doctors. EVAde is built on one design rule from our whiteboard: we do not assume astronauts know how to assess their health.

  • Collects health indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, mood, symptoms, meals, hydration and radiation dose.
  • Compares each reading with standard reference ranges and with the astronaut's own recent history, because spaceflight studies are small (n = 1 to 25) and individuals vary.
  • Explains every flag: green, yellow or red, why it fired, and what to do now.
  • Escalates concerns to a flight-surgeon downlink queue that models three link states: online (ISS), a 20-minute Mars delay, and a blackout that holds messages until the link returns.
  • Watches space weather: NOAA ≥10 MeV proton flux at or above 10 pfu (NOAA S1 radiation storm) means a spacewalk is no-go.

How it works

  • Web app (https://evade.health). React 19 + TypeScript (Vite) with pages for Dashboard (vitals, sleep, mood, radiation against the 600 mSv career limit, bone, cardio, immune, nutrition), Tasks (a gamified daily health checklist), Journal (with voice check-in), Tutorials and Selfies (photo log). The dashboard currently shows simulated demo crew data and is labelled "demo data only."
  • Voice check-in. An astronaut calls the Twilio phone line or opens the journal in a browser. A Cloudflare Worker hands the audio to a Durable Object, which bridges it to xAI Grok realtime voice. The agent asks about sleep, mood, symptoms and vitals, then calls two tools: save_checkin stores the check-in in Cloudflare D1, rates it green/yellow/red with reasons and actions, and compares sleep and mood with the astronaut's last 7 check-ins; queue_flight_surgeon_message adds a message to the downlink queue in online, Mars or blackout mode. Twilio webhooks are signature-checked, and a token-protected endpoint can place an outbound red-alert call.
  • Cloud API (https://api.evade.health). A second Cloudflare Worker with a D1 database holds users, 41 health metric definitions, observations, personal baselines, self-reports, journal entries, alerts, tasks, meals and hydration. A Cron Trigger pulls NOAA space weather every 15 minutes. Crew sign in through Cloudflare Access, and roles separate astronauts (own data only) from flight surgeons, therapists and admins. A Durable Object provides a live crew feed over WebSockets. xAI Grok powers journal summaries, the EVA companion and voice-to-text. Concerning journal language always raises a red alert through a keyword check that the AI cannot override.
  • Health logic is a hybrid on purpose. Fixed rules plus the personal baseline decide what is critical, so a flight surgeon can trust and audit them. Machine-learning models are only used to find patterns (such as stress or fatigue from EEG/ECG) and never decide on their own that something is critical.
  • Python tools. The evade_space package seeds demo crew, models daily radiation dose by environment (station, spacecraft, planetary base, rover) against NASA's limits, and finds safe spacewalk windows from the NOAA Kp forecast and proton flux.

Key benefits

  • Personal, not population. Each astronaut is measured against their own baseline, and the baseline can be re-learned in flight (resting EEG alpha power drops after launch and stays low for weeks).
  • Explainable. Every alert gives a reason and concrete steps; nothing critical is decided by a black-box model.
  • Hands-free. A voice check-in works by phone or browser, without typing.
  • Built for distance. The downlink queue already models the 3 to 22 minute Mars delay and solar-conjunction blackouts.
  • Honest numbers. Every value in our research catalog carries an evidence label: backed (from a study), derived (our arithmetic on a study's value), modelled, or illustrative (chosen for a demo).
  • Decision support, not a medical device. EVAde says so in the app and in the voice agent.

Goals

  • Wire the web app to api.evade.health so the dashboard shows real check-ins, baselines and alerts.
  • Deploy the ECG/EEG models trained on public lab datasets (SAM40, WESAD) and report cross-validated accuracy on real data.
  • Add NASA DONKI solar-particle-event replay, and draw on NASA OSDR (Inspiration4) and LSDA data.
  • Build the flight-surgeon and therapist admin panel, and an on-device text-to-speech path for Mars, where a live voice link is not possible.

Tools & technologies

  • Languages: TypeScript, Python, SQL.
  • Frontend: React 19, Vite, react-router, Recharts, Astryx design system, Heroicons.
  • Cloud (Cloudflare): Workers, D1, Durable Objects, Workers KV, Cron Triggers, Cloudflare Access, Custom Domains, Workers Observability, Wrangler.
  • Voice: Twilio Programmable Voice and Media Streams; xAI Grok realtime voice (grok-voice-latest).
  • Backend and models: Python FastAPI and uvicorn (original voice agent and the model service).
  • Testing: Vitest with the Cloudflare Workers pool, pytest.
  • Domain: evade.health, registered with GoDaddy, with DNS on Cloudflare.
  • Hardware: none built. The demo runs on a laptop browser and microphone or any phone. The indicators are designed for sensors astronauts already use or could use (ECG chest patch, blood-pressure cuff, glucose monitor, core-temperature sensor, personal dosimeter), which are simulated in this demo.
